title: Characterization of the Localization of Vaginal Intraepithelial Neoplasia (VaIN): A Retrospective Data Analysis
summary:
Knowing where VaIN lesions are most likely to occur is important for their diagnosis. The cervix has a surface area of about 4–8 cm², while the surface of the vagina is more than ten times larger and contains many folds and small recesses. Therefore, finding vaginal lesions during colposcopy can be difficult.
The aim of this study is to determine where VaIN lesions are most commonly located. We will map the location of the lesions to investigate whether there are specific areas of the vagina where VaIN occurs more frequently.

interventions.name:
Retrospective analysis of all patients from 2014 to 2024 in whom vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN) was detected during differential colposcopy and the respective location of the lesion was documented.
